title: Deadlifting with a Mixed Grip, Straps or a Hook Grip Is for Egomaniacs and Cheat
summary: NH rebuts a Natty or Not article claiming only double-overhand deadlifts are legitimate. He argues grip strength depends mostly on hand size, that letting grip cap posterior chain work sacrifices tonnage and growth, that straps are safe and not cheating, and that the mixed grip carries real biceps-tear risk.
claims: Calling straps or heavy lifting 'ego' is an appeal to emotion used to shame people
Cheating doesn't exist outside rules; a cheat curl is still a lift if it serves your goals
'No straps in the jungle' is hypocritical since powerlifting itself has weight classes
A hook grip is like straps using your body as the hook
Powerlifters reject straps for deadlifts but use them for shrugs and rows, and depend on belts and sleeves anyway
Double overhand, then mixed or hook grip, is dogma from powerlifting rules and makes no sense for hypertrophy
Much deadlift grip failure comes from the bar rolling and prying fingers open; a mixed grip stops the roll
He mixed-gripped deadlifts for two years for no reason; it didn't grow his forearms
Check everything you do for synergy and specificity with the rest of your training; if it doesn't fit, rethink it
The hook grip is mostly a finger-strength demand
Find each lift's limiting factor and remove it; that's why straps are so good
If you can bypass a supposed injury-prevention mechanism without getting hurt, it wasn't one; grip isn't a safety mechanism
Pain is not the same as injury; pain is often a warning
Grip strength depends far more on hand size and finger length than forearm strength; grip champions have huge hands
He has big palms and short fingers and thumbs, which makes his grip terrible
Double overhand would cap his deadlift around 330 for a single and under 300 for reps, while he now deadlifts 470
Letting the small forearm muscles limit the much bigger hamstrings, glutes and back is idiotic; nobody holds a back squat with the hands
People get hurt deadlifting from poor form and poor intensity control, not straps; strongmen pull 1000 lb with straps without forearm or wrist injuries
Letting grip lower stress on the body lowers tonnage and therefore gains; stress isn't bad in itself
Gym rules about quiet, controlled lowering exist to protect equipment, not lifters
Low bar, bulldog grips and similar adaptations are legitimate ways to use the most muscle safely
The mixed grip isn't a good grip and genuinely risks a biceps tear, especially when lifters curl the bar as grip fails
Calling people low IQ is a weak argument; IQ tests vary by culture and miss other forms of intelligence
His short fingers make hook grip impossible, so in competition he'd have to mixed grip, like Chris Duffin
Mixed grip gave him only some nucleus overload in his left biceps
Bodybuilders have no reason to hook grip; use straps
Banning grips in powerlifting would drop world records about 50% and kill the sport
Small hands limit grip volume and so forearm growth: a vicious circle
Grip and forearm muscle are different entities; forearms grow through wrist flexion and isometric holds
Sacrificing 10-30% of deadlift tonnage would make him shrink
Low bar can save tall, lanky lifters who can't hold thoracic extension in high bar, keeping the bar over midfoot with a better torso angle
Smart long-career powerlifters choose repeatable, injury-preventing methods
Injury risk doesn't rise with intensity as much as people think if technique is good and volume and intensity follow recovery
Weight on the bar is never worthless as long as it reflects progression
exercises: removes grip limit to load posterior chain
needs long fingers; pointless for bodybuilders
keeps tall lifters' bar over midfoot
